00001| ---
00002| title: route.js
00003| description: API reference for the route.js special file.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.
00007| 
00008| ```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
00009| export async function GET() {
00010|   return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })
00011| }
00012| ```
00013| 
00014| ```js filename="route.js" switcher
00015| export async function GET() {
00016|   return Response.json({ message: 'Hello World' })
00017| }
00018| ```
00019| 
00020| ## Reference
00021| 
00022| ### HTTP Methods
00023| 
00024| A **route** file allows you to create custom request handlers for a given route. The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`.
00025| 
00026| ```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
00027| export async function GET(request: Request) {}
00028| 
00029| export async function HEAD(request: Request) {}
00030| 
00031| export async function POST(request: Request) {}
00032| 
00033| export async function PUT(request: Request) {}
00034| 
00035| export async function DELETE(request: Request) {}
00036| 
00037| export async function PATCH(request: Request) {}
00038| 
00039| // If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
00040| export async function OPTIONS(request: Request) {}
00041| ```
00042| 
00043| ```js filename="route.js" switcher
00044| export async function GET(request) {}
00045| 
00046| export async function HEAD(request) {}
00047| 
00048| export async function POST(request) {}
00049| 
00050| export async function PUT(request) {}
00051| 
00052| export async function DELETE(request) {}
00053| 
00054| export async function PATCH(request) {}
00055| 
00056| // If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
00057| export async function OPTIONS(request) {}
00058| ```
00059| 
00060| ### Parameters
00061| 
00062| #### `request` (optional)
00063| 
00064| The `request` object is a [NextRequest](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) object, which is an extension of the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) API. `NextRequest` gives you further control over the incoming request, including easily accessing `cookies` and an extended, parsed, URL object `nextUrl`.
00065| 
00066| ```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
00067| import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
00068| 
00069| export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
00070|   const url = request.nextUrl
00071| }
00072| ```
00073| 
00074| ```js filename="route.js" switcher
00075| export async function GET(request) {
00076|   const url = request.nextUrl
00077| }
00078| ```
00079| 
00080| #### `context` (optional)
00081| 
00082| - **`params`**: a promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) for the current route.
00083| 
00084| ```ts filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.ts" switcher
00085| export async function GET(
00086|   request: Request,
00087|   { params }: { params: Promise<{ team: string }> }
00088| ) {
00089|   const { team } = await params
00090| }
00091| ```
00092| 
00093| ```js filename="app/dashboard/[team]/route.js" switcher
00094| export async function GET(request, { params }) {
00095|   const { team } = await params
00096| }
00097| ```
00098| 
00099| | Example                          | URL            | `params`                           |
00100| | -------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
00101| | `app/dashboard/[team]/route.js`  | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>`           |
00102| | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/route.js` | `/shop/1/2`    | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` |
00103| | `app/blog/[...slug]/route.js`    | `/blog/1/2`    | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>`    |
00104| 
00105| ### Route Context Helper
00106| 
00107| You can type the Route Handler context using `RouteContext` to get strongly typed `params` from a route literal. `RouteContext` is a globally available helper.
00108| 
00109| ```ts filename="app/users/[id]/route.ts"
00110| import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
00111| 
00112| export async function GET(_req: NextRequest, ctx: RouteContext<'/users/[id]'>) {
00113|   const { id } = await ctx.params
00114|   return Response.json({ id })
00115| }
00116| ```
00117| 
00118| > **Good to know**
00119| >
00120| > - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`.
00121| > - After type generation, the `RouteContext` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported.
00122| 
00123| ## Examples
00124| 
00125| ### Cookies
00126| 
00127| You can read or set cookies with [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) from `next/headers`.
00128| 
00129| ```ts filename="route.ts" switcher
00130| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00131| 
00132| export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
00133|   const cookieStore = await cookies()
00134| 
00135|   const a = cookieStore.get('a')
00136|   const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1')
00137|   const c = cookieStore.delete('c')
00138| }
00139| ```
00140| 
00141| ```js filename="route.js" switcher
00142| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00143| 
00144| export async function GET(request) {
00145|   const cookieStore = await cookies()
00146| 
00147|   const a = cookieStore.get('a')
00148|   const b = cookieStore.set('b', '1')
00149|   const c = cookieStore.delete('c')
00150| }
00151| ```
00152| 
00153| Alternatively, you can return a new `Response` using the [`Set-Cookie`](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie) header.
00154| 
00155| ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher
00156| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00157| 
00158| export async function GET(request: Request) {
00159|   const cookieStore = await cookies()
00160|   const token = cookieStore.get('token')
00161| 
00162|   return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', {
00163|     status: 200,
00164|     headers: { 'Set-Cookie': `token=${token.value}` },
00165|   })
00166| }
00167| ```
00168| 
00169| ```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher
00170| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00171| 
00172| export async function GET(request) {
00173|   const cookieStore = await cookies()
00174|   const token = cookieStore.get('token')
00175| 
00176|   return new Response('Hello, Next.js!', {
00177|     status: 200,
00178|     headers: { 'Set-Cookie': `token=${token.value}` },
00179|   })
00180| }
00181| ```
00182| 
00183| You can also use the underlying Web APIs to read cookies from the request ([`NextRequest`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request)):
00184| 
00185| ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher
00186| import { type NextRequest } from 'next/server'
00187| 
00188| export async function GET(request: NextRequest) {
00189|   const token = request.cookies.get('token')
00190| }
00191| ```
00192| 
00193| ```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher
00194| export async function GET(request) {
00195|   const token = request.cookies.get('token')
00196| }
00197| ```

00006| Route Handlers allow you to create custom request handlers for a given route using the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs.

00011| }
00012| ```
00013|

00018| ```

00020| ## Reference
00021| 
00022| ### HTTP Methods
00023| 
00024| A **route** file allows you to create custom request handlers for a given route. The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`.

00026| ```ts filename="route.ts" switcher

00028| 
00029| export async function HEAD(request: Request) {}
00030| 
00031| export async function POST(request: Request) {}
00032| 
00033| export async function PUT(request: Request) {}
00034| 
00035| export async function DELETE(request: Request) {}
00036| 
00037| export async function PATCH(request: Request) {}
00038| 
00039| // If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
00040| export async function OPTIONS(request: Request) {}
00041| ```
00042|

00044| export async function GET(request) {}
00045| 
00046| export async function HEAD(request) {}
00047| 
00048| export async function POST(request) {}
00049| 
00050| export async function PUT(request) {}
00051| 
00052| export async function DELETE(request) {}
00053| 
00054| export async function PATCH(request) {}
00055| 
00056| // If `OPTIONS` is not defined, Next.js will automatically implement `OPTIONS` and set the appropriate Response `Allow` header depending on the other methods defined in the Route Handler.
00057| export async function OPTIONS(request) {}
00058| ```
00059| 
00060| ### Parameters
00061| 
00062| #### `request` (optional)
00063| 
00064| The `request` object is a [NextRequest](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) object, which is an extension of the Web [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) API. `NextRequest` gives you further control over the incoming request, including easily accessing `cookies` and an extended, parsed, URL object `nextUrl`.

00071| }
00072| ```
00073|

00077| }
00078| ```

00090| }
00091| ```

00096| }
00097| ```

00003| description: API reference for the layout.js file.
00004| ---
00005| 
00006| The `layout` file is used to define a layout in your Next.js application.
00007| 
00008| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher
00009| export default function DashboardLayout({
00010|   children,
00011| }: {
00012|   children: React.ReactNode
00013| }) {
00014|   return <section>{children}</section>
00015| }
00016| ```
00017| 
00018| ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.js" switcher
00019| export default function DashboardLayout({ children }) {
00020|   return <section>{children}</section>
00021| }
00022| ```
00023| 
00024| In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `layout.js` is the outermost component in a route segment. It wraps `template.js`, `error.js`, `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, and `page.js`.
00025| 
00026| A **root layout** is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. It is used to define the `<html>` and `<body>` tags and other globally shared UI.
00027| 
00028| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00029| export default function RootLayout({
00030|   children,
00031| }: {
00032|   children: React.ReactNode
00033| }) {
00034|   return (
00035|     <html lang="en">
00036|       <body>{children}</body>
00037|     </html>
00038|   )
00039| }
00040| ```
00041| 
00042| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00043| export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
00044|   return (
00045|     <html lang="en">
00046|       <body>{children}</body>
00047|     </html>
00048|   )
00049| }
00050| ```
00051| 
00052| ## Reference
00053| 
00054| ### Props
00055| 
00056| #### `children` (required)
00057| 
00058| Layout components should accept and use a `children` prop. During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. These will primarily be the component of a child [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (if it exists) or [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), but could also be other special files like [Loading](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) or [Error](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling) when applicable.
00059| 
00060| #### `params` (optional)
00061| 
00062| A promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to that layout.
00063| 
00064| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.tsx" switcher
00065| export default async function Layout({
00066|   children,
00067|   params,
00068| }: {
00069|   children: React.ReactNode
00070|   params: Promise<{ team: string }>
00071| }) {
00072|   const { team } = await params
00073| }
00074| ```
00075| 
00076| ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js" switcher
00077| export default async function Layout({ children, params }) {
00078|   const { team } = await params
00079| }
00080| ```
00081| 
00082| | Example Route                     | URL            | `params`                           |
00083| | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- |
00084| | `app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js`  | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>`           |
00085| | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/layout.js` | `/shop/1/2`    | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` |
00086| | `app/blog/[...slug]/layout.js`    | `/blog/1/2`    | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>`    |
00087| 
00088| - Since the `params` prop is a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values.
00089|   - In version 14 and earlier, `params` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future.
00090| 
00091| ### Layout Props Helper
00092| 
00093| You can type layouts with `LayoutProps` to get a strongly typed `params` and named slots inferred from your directory structure. `LayoutProps` is a globally available helper.
00094| 
00095| ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx"
00096| export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<'/dashboard'>) {
00097|   return (
00098|     <section>
00099|       {props.children}
00100|       {/* If you have app/dashboard/@analytics, it appears as a typed slot: */}
00101|       {/* {props.analytics} */}
00102|     </section>
00103|   )
00104| }
00105| ```
00106| 
00107| > **Good to know**:
00108| >
00109| > - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`.
00110| > - After type generation, the `LayoutProps` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported.
00111| 
00112| ### Root Layout
00113| 
00114| The `app` directory **must** include a **root layout**, which is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. Typically, the root layout is `app/layout.js`.
00115| 
00116| ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
00117| export default function RootLayout({
00118|   children,
00119| }: {
00120|   children: React.ReactNode
00121| }) {
00122|   return (
00123|     <html>
00124|       <body>{children}</body>
00125|     </html>
00126|   )
00127| }
00128| ```
00129| 
00130| ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
00131| export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
00132|   return (
00133|     <html>
00134|       <body>{children}</body>
00135|     </html>
00136|   )
00137| }
00138| ```
00139| 
00140| - The root layout **must** define `<html>` and `<body>` tags.
00141|   - You should **not** manually add `<head>` tags such as `<title>` and `<meta>` to root layouts. Instead, you should use the [Metadata API](/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images) which automatically handles advanced requirements such as streaming and de-duplicating `<head>` elements.
00142| - You can create **multiple root layouts**. Any layout without a `layout.js` above it is a root layout. Two common approaches:
00143|   - Using [route groups](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-groups) like `app/(shop)/layout.js` and `app/(marketing)/layout.js`
00144|   - Omitting `app/layout.js` so layouts in subdirectories like `app/dashboard/layout.js` and `app/blog/layout.js` each become root layouts for their respective directories.
00145|   - Navigating **across multiple root layouts** will cause a **full page load** (as opposed to a client-side navigation).
00146| - The root layout can be under a **dynamic segment**, for example when implementing [internationalization](/docs/app/guides/internationalization) with `app/[lang]/layout.js`. Dynamic segments before the root layout are **root parameters** and can be read from any Server Component with [`next/root-params`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params).
00147| 
00148| ## Caveats
00149| 
00150| ### Request Object
00151| 
00152| Layouts are cached in the client during navigation to avoid unnecessary server requests.
00153| 
00154| [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) do not rerender. They can be cached and reused to avoid unnecessary computation when navigating between pages. By restricting layouts from accessing the raw request, Next.js can prevent the execution of potentially slow or expensive user code within the layout, which could negatively impact performance.
00155| 
00156| To access the request object, you can use [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) APIs in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) and Functions.
00157| 
00158| ```tsx filename="app/shop/layout.tsx" switcher
00159| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00160| 
00161| export default async function Layout({ children }) {
00162|   const cookieStore = await cookies()
00163|   const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
00164|   return '...'
00165| }
00166| ```
00167| 
00168| ```jsx filename="app/shop/layout.js" switcher
00169| import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
00170| 
00171| export default async function Layout({ children }) {
00172|   const cookieStore = await cookies()
00173|   const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
00174|   return '...'
00175| }
00176| ```
00177| 
00178| ### Query params

00180| Layouts do not rerender on navigation, so they cannot access search params which would otherwise become stale.
00181| 
00182| To access updated query parameters, you can use the Page [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) prop, or read them inside a Client Component using the [`useSearchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) hook. Since Client Components re-render on navigation, they have access to the latest query parameters.

00195| }

title: not-found.js
description: API reference for the not-found.js file.

Next.js provides two conventions to handle not found cases:

- **`not-found.js`**: Used when you call the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function in a route segment.
- **`global-not-found.js`**: Used to define a global 404 page for unmatched routes across your entire app. This is handled at the routing level and doesn't depend on rendering a layout or page.

## `not-found.js`

The **not-found** file is used to render UI when the [`notFound`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) function is thrown within a route segment. Along with serving a custom UI, Next.js will return a `200` HTTP status code for streamed responses, and `404` for non-streamed responses (see [Status Codes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#status-codes) for details about SEO).

00014| You can use the `metadata` object or the `generateMetadata` function to define metadata.
00015| 
00016| ## The `metadata` object
00017| 
00018| To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields) from a `layout.js` or `page.js` file.
00019| 
00020| ```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
00021| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00022| 
00023| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00024|   title: '...',
00025|   description: '...',
00026| }
00027| 
00028| export default function Page() {}
00029| ```
00030| 
00031| ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher
00032| export const metadata = {
00033|   title: '...',
00034|   description: '...',
00035| }
00036| 
00037| export default function Page() {}
00038| ```
00039| 
00040| > See the [Metadata Fields](#metadata-fields) for a complete list of supported options.
00041| 
00042| ## `generateMetadata` function
00043| 
00044| Dynamic metadata depends on **dynamic information**, such as the current route parameters, external data, or `metadata` in parent segments, can be set by exporting a `generateMetadata` function that returns a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields).
00045| 
00046| Resolving `generateMetadata` is part of rendering the page. If the page can be prerendered and `generateMetadata` doesn't introduce dynamic behavior, the resulting metadata is included in the page's initial HTML.
00047| 
00048| Otherwise the metadata resolved from `generateMetadata` [can be streamed](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata) after sending the initial UI.
00049| 
00050| ```tsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
00051| import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
00052| 
00053| type Props = {
00054|   params: Promise<{ id: string }>
00055|   searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
00056| }
00057| 
00058| export async function generateMetadata(
00059|   { params, searchParams }: Props,
00060|   parent: ResolvingMetadata
00061| ): Promise<Metadata> {
00062|   // read route params
00063|   const { id } = await params
00064| 
00065|   // fetch data
00066|   const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
00067| 
00068|   // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
00069|   const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
00070| 
00071|   return {
00072|     title: product.title,
00073|     openGraph: {
00074|       images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
00075|     },
00076|   }
00077| }
00078| 
00079| export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
00080| ```
00081| 
00082| ```jsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.js" switcher
00083| export async function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }, parent) {
00084|   // read route params
00085|   const { id } = await params
00086| 
00087|   // fetch data
00088|   const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
00089| 
00090|   // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
00091|   const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
00092| 
00093|   return {
00094|     title: product.title,
00095|     openGraph: {
00096|       images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
00097|     },
00098|   }
00099| }
00100| 
00101| export default function Page({ params, searchParams }) {}
00102| ```
00103| 
00104| For type completion of `params` and `searchParams`, you can type the first argument with [`PageProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`LayoutProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper) for pages and layouts respectively.
00105| 
00106| > **Good to know**:
00107| >
00108| > - Metadata can be added to `layout.js` and `page.js` files.
00109| > - Next.js will automatically resolve the metadata, and create the relevant `<head>` tags for the page.
00110| > - The `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function exports are **only supported in Server Components**.
00111| > - You cannot export both the `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function from the same route segment.
00112| > - `fetch` requests inside `generateMetadata` are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components.
00113| > - React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
00114| > - [File-based metadata](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata) has the higher priority and will override the `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function.
00115| 
00116| ## Why `generateMetadata` is Server Component only
00117| 
00118| `generateMetadata` and the `metadata` export are only supported in Server Components because metadata must be resolved on the server before the page component is rendered. This allows Next.js to include the metadata in the initial HTML response.
00119| 
00120| If you need to use Client Component features, keep your `page.tsx` as a Server Component and move the Client Component logic to a separate file:
00121| 
00122| ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
00123| import type { Metadata } from 'next'
00124| import { InteractiveComponent } from './interactive-component'
00125| 
00126| export const metadata: Metadata = {
00127|   title: 'My Page',
00128| }
00129| 
00130| export default function Page() {
00131|   return <InteractiveComponent />
00132| }
00133| ```
00134| 
00135| ```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
00136| import { InteractiveComponent } from './interactive-component'
00137| 
00138| export const metadata = {
00139|   title: 'My Page',
00140| }
00141| 
00142| export default function Page() {
00143|   return <InteractiveComponent />
00144| }
00145| ```
00146| 
00147| ```tsx filename="app/interactive-component.tsx" switcher
00148| 'use client'
00149| 
00150| export function InteractiveComponent() {
00151|   // Client-side interactivity (hooks, event handlers, etc.)
00152| }
00153| ```
00154| 
00155| ```jsx filename="app/interactive-component.js" switcher
00156| 'use client'
00157| 
00158| export function InteractiveComponent() {
00159|   // Client-side interactivity (hooks, event handlers, etc.)
00160| }
00161| ```

00166| 
00167| `generateMetadata` function accepts the following parameters:
00168| 
00169| - `props` - An object containing the parameters of the current route:
00170|   - `params` - An object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to the segment `generateMetadata` is called from. Examples:
00171| 
00172|     | Route                           | URL         | `params`                  |
00173|     | ------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------- |
00174|     | `app/shop/[slug]/page.js`       | `/shop/1`   | `{ slug: '1' }`           |
00175|     | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/page.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `{ tag: '1', item: '2' }` |
00176|     | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js`    | `/shop/1/2` | `{ slug: ['1', '2'] }`    |

00183|     | `/shop?a=1&b=2` | `{ a: '1', b: '2' }` |
00184|     | `/shop?a=1&a=2` | `{ a: ['1', '2'] }`  |
00185| 
00186| - `parent` - A promise of the resolved metadata from parent route segments.

A URL path is a sequence of path segments. In the App Router, a segment may be **static** (a literal value matched exactly) or **dynamic** (a placeholder that captures a value from the URL). When you don't know a segment's value ahead of time, define a Dynamic Segment to create routes from dynamic data. Next.js passes the captured values to your page via the path `params` prop, either filled in at request time or prerendered at build time.

> **Good to know**: Dynamic Segments are often referred to as path params, route params, or URL params.

A Dynamic Segment can be created by wrapping a folder's name in square brackets: `[folderName]`. For example, a blog could include the following route `app/blog/[slug]/page.js` where `[slug]` is the Dynamic Segment for blog posts.

00017|

00043| 
00044| - `router.push(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route. Adds a new entry into the [browser's history stack](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/History_API). The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
00045| - `router.replace(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route without adding a new entry into the browser’s history stack. The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
00046| - `router.refresh()`: Refresh the current route. Making a new request to the server, re-fetching data requests, and re-rendering Server Components. The client will merge the updated React Server Component payload without losing unaffected client-side React (e.g. `useState`) or browser state (e.g. scroll position). This clears the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache) for the current route, but does **not** invalidate the server-side cache. Use [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to invalidate server-side cached data.
00047| - `router.prefetch(href: string, options?: { onInvalidate?: () => void })`: [Prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) the provided route for faster client-side transitions. The optional `onInvalidate` callback is called when the [prefetched data becomes stale](/docs/app/guides/prefetching#extending-or-ejecting-link).

00049| - `router.forward()`: Navigate forwards to the next page in the browser’s history stack.

/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

00182|  * @returns {Promise<import('../plugin/contract.js').RunnerResult>}
00183|  */
00184| export async function runAgent(input) {
00185|   const args = buildOpenCodeCliArgs(input);
00186| 
00187|   // spawnSync (not a shell string): the prompt is a plain argv element, so there
00188|   // is no shell quoting/escaping to get wrong. Blocking is fine — the runner has
00189|   // nothing else to do while the agent works. The sandbox-level timeout bounds it.
00190|   const res = spawnSync('opencode', args, {
00191|     cwd: input.cwd,
00192|     env: process.env,
00193|     encoding: 'utf8',
00194|     maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
00195|   });
00196| 
00197|   const stdout = res.stdout || '';
00198|   const stderr = res.stderr || '';
00199|   // Preserve the old concatenation order: stdout THEN stderr.
00200|   const output = stdout + stderr;
00201|   // spawnSync sets status=null + error when the binary can't be spawned at all.
00202|   const agentExitCode = res.status == null ? -1 : res.status;
00203| 
00204|   // Capture the transcript from the combined output (old: over stdout+stderr).
00205|   const transcript = extractTranscriptFromOutput(output) ?? null;
00206| 
00207|   // Resolve the model OpenCode actually used. The `--format json` events never
00208|   // include it, so first try scraping the printed logs (works on OpenCode <=
00209|   // 1.16.x), then fall back to `opencode export <sessionID>`, whose assistant
00210|   // messages carry providerID/modelID (OpenCode 1.17.0 changed the log format,
00211|   // which broke the scrape). Observation must never fail the run.
00212|   let observedModel = extractObservedModelFromOpenCodeOutput(output);
00213|   if (!observedModel) {
00214|     const sessionId = extractSessionIdFromTranscript(transcript ?? undefined);
00215|     if (sessionId) {
00216|       try {
00217|         const exportRes = spawnSync('opencode', ['export', sessionId], {
00218|           cwd: input.cwd,
00219|           env: process.env,
00220|           encoding: 'utf8',
00221|           maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024,
00222|         });
00223|         if ((exportRes.status == null ? -1 : exportRes.status) === 0) {
00224|           observedModel = extractObservedModelFromSessionExport(exportRes.stdout || '');
00225|         }
00226|       } catch {
00227|         // Leave observedModel undefined.
00228|       }
00229|     }
00230|   }
00231|   const observedModelOrNull = observedModel ?? null;
00232| 
00233|   if (res.error || agentExitCode !== 0) {
00234|     // Mirror the old error string: last 5 lines of output, else a coded fallback.
00235|     const errorLines = output.trim().split('\n').slice(-5).join('\n');
00236|     const fallback = res.error
00237|       ? `Failed to run opencode: ${res.error.message}`
00238|       : `OpenCode CLI exited with code ${agentExitCode}`;
00239|     return {
00240|       ok: false,
00241|       output,
00242|       transcript,
00243|       observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00244|       error: errorLines || fallback,
00245|       agentExitCode,
00246|     };
00247|   }
00248| 
00249|   return {
00250|     ok: true,
00251|     output,
00252|     transcript,
00253|     observedModel: observedModelOrNull,
00254|     error: null,
00255|     agentExitCode,
00256|   };
00257| }
00258| 
00259| /* ─────────────────────────── runnable (CLI) entry ─────────────────────────── */
00260| 
00261| // True when this file is executed directly (`node run.mjs ...`), false when imported.
00262| const isMain = process.argv[1] && fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) === process.argv[1];
00263| 
00264| if (isMain) {

00266|   const input = JSON.parse(process.argv[2]);
00267| 
00268|   // Always produce a RunnerResult, even if the runner itself throws, so the host
00269|   // always has a result file to read (node exit code stays 0 except on a truly
00270|   // unrecoverable crash before we can write).
00271|   let result;
00272|   try {
00273|     result = await runAgent(input);
00274|   } catch (e) {
00275|     result = {
00276|       ok: false,
00277|       output: '',
00278|       transcript: null,
00279|       observedModel: null,
00280|       error: e && e.message ? e.message : String(e),
00281|       agentExitCode: -1,
00282|     };
00283|   }
00284| 
00285|   // Source of truth: the result file the host reads back via sandbox.readFile.
00286|   try {
00287|     mkdirSync(dirname(input.resultPath), { recursive: true });
00288|     writeFileSync(input.resultPath, JSON.stringify(result));
00289|   } catch {
00290|     // If the file can't be written, the host falls back to the marker line below.
00291|   }
00292| 
00293|   // Fallback channel: a compact status line (no transcript — it can be huge).
00294|   process.stdout.write(
00295|     '__AGENT_RESULT__ ' +
00296|       JSON.stringify({
00297|         ok: result.ok,
00298|         observedModel: result.observedModel,
00299|         error: result.error,
00300|         agentExitCode: result.agentExitCode,
00301|       }) +
00302|       '\n'
00303|   );
00304| 
00305|   // Exit 0: "the runner ran". Agent success/failure is conveyed via result.ok, not
00306|   // the node exit code (the host distinguishes the two).
00307|   process.exit(0);
00308| }

/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
